Restore-failed dsh row scored as ordinary

label: The scorer never reads restored or headMoved: a run is scored whenever its session loads, whatever exit the turn ended with, and the exit code never decides a score.
Capped is true for two different events: exit code 143, or exit code null.

The two causes split by runtime in 033: opencode 26 capped lines are all exit 143 (15 off, 11 on), devin 19 are all exit null (10 off, 9 on), pi 2 off and 0 on are 143, and claude and dsh have none, so the printed capped column compares unlike events.

Devin exit-null lines are mostly not restore faults: all 19 carry restored true, none carries headMoved, only 2 are the fresh-skill-04 restore-failed lines, so a missing exit code alone labels a turn capped.

A capped start row leaves the start-rate denominator and is counted apart, so devin printed start rate rests on 11 and 12 judgeable rows of 15 because its exit code was never recorded rather than because the turns were slow.

The row the runner calls unmeasurable is scored as an ordinary row: dsh restore-failed fresh-skill-04 carries exit 0, passes every filter and counts in the dsh block, while reruns.txt records the same row as not rerun and unmeasurable.
